defects.description: The text says the number of people in cities 'overtook' the number in the countryside around 2007, yet describes the urban share as 'less than half' — overtaking means the urban share became the majority (more than half).
paraphrases: If urban overtook rural, the urban share must exceed half, not be less than half.
'Less than half' contradicts the claim that cities overtook the countryside.
Overtaking rural implies a majority, so 'less than half' is wrong.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'more than half' (overtaking = majority). Findable within the same sentence, distinct.

defects.description: In 1960 the rural population is said to be 'more than 60%', which leaves under 40% urban, but the text says 'over 40% in towns and cities'.
paraphrases: If rural was over 60%, urban must be under 40%, not over 40%.
The urban and rural shares would exceed 100% (over 60% plus over 40%).
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'under 40%' (complement of >60%). Findable from the rural figure in the same sentence, distinct.

defects.description: The breakdown gives 45% cities, 35% towns, and 40% villages, which sums to 120% rather than 100%.
paraphrases: The three shares do not add up to the whole population.
The village share should make the parts total 100%.
defects.rationale: Correct value '20% live in villages' (45 + 35 + 20 = 100). Findable from the three shares, distinct from the other defects.
